items.title: macOS: Fn/Globe key (keyCode 63) swallowed by WKWebView before reaching IME — IME voice shortcuts fail in Wails apps

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
## Summary

On macOS, the **Fn / Globe key (`keyCode 63`) is swallowed by WKWebView before it ever reaches the input method**, so any IME feature triggered by holding Fn (e.g. voice input / push-to-talk shortcuts in Chinese input methods like 豆包输入法/DoubaoIme) silently fails **inside every Wails app window**, while the same IME works fine in native apps and Chromium apps.

## Environment

- macOS 26.2, Apple Silicon (arm64)
- Wails app: Reasonix Desktop (Wails/WKWebView variant, v1.31.4, `com.wails.reasonix-desktop`) — but this affects **any** Wails app on macOS
- IME: DoubaoIme (豆包输入法), voice shortcut bound to "hold Fn/Globe"

## Observed behavior

| Target | Pressing Fn (physical or remapped) while IME voice input is active |
|---|---|
| Native app (e.g. TextEdit, SwiftUI app) | ✅ IME receives the key, voice input starts |
| Chromium app (Chrome, Codex desktop) | ✅ works |
| **Wails app (WKWebView)** | ❌ IME never receives it — no reaction at all |

Typing in the Wails app works fine (`keyDown` path → `NSTextInputContext` → IME). The problem is specific to the **bare Fn modifier event**: it arrives as `flagsChanged` and is dropped.

## Root cause (upstream WebKit)

WebKit's `WebViewImpl::flagsChanged()` explicitly filters `keyCode 63` (Fn/Globe) and returns **before** calling `interpretKeyEvent()` (the call that hands the event to the current `NSTextInputContext` / IME):

- https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/mac/WebViewImpl.mm#L5916-L5920
- https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebKit/UIProcess/mac/WebViewImpl.mm#L6826-L6840

Chinese IMEs commonly use "hold Fn/Globe to speak" as a voice shortcut, and hardware remappers (e.g. turning a Bluetooth remote's mic button into Fn) produce exactly this event, so both physical and remapped Fn fail.

## Request

Please consider a macOS-side fix in Wails so Fn/Globe events are forwarded to the input context instead of being silently dropped, e.g. install a `NSEventMaskFlagsChanged` local monitor on the Wails window that, for `keyCode 63`, forwards the event to the current first responder's `[inputContext handleEvent:event]` while still passing the original event through to AppKit (per Apple's `NSTextInputContext.handleEvent` docs: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nstextinputcontext/handleevent(_:)).

A WebKit-upstream fix would be "deliver Fn to the IME while still not generating a DOM keyboard event".

## Minimal repro

1. Install any Chinese IME that supports a "hold Fn to speak" voice shortcut (e.g. DoubaoIme) and bind its voice key to Fn/Globe.
2. Open any Wails app, focus a text field, and make sure the IME is active.
3. Hold Fn and speak → nothing happens.
4. Repeat in TextEdit or Chrome → works.

## Related

- Wails v3 Chinese-input issues (closed, different symptom): #4550, #2933

items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Currently, a message dialog usage looks like the code below where the callback per button are asynchronous.

```
        app.Dialog.Question().
            SetTitle("Migration Warning").
            SetMessage(fmt.Sprintf("%d migrations are available. Do you want to run them now?", len(pending))).
            SetDefaultButton(&application.Button{
                Label: "Run",
                IsCancel: false,
                IsDefault: true,
                Callback: func() {
                    doMigrations()
                },
            }).
            SetCancelButton(&application.Button{
                Label: "Cancel",
                IsCancel: true,
                IsDefault: false,
                Callback: func() {
                    log.Println("Migration cancelled by user.")
                },
            }).
            Show()    
```

The challenge with this pattern is that, there is no way of returning error or result from each `callback` function synchronously so that the application can take critical decisions such as exiting the application if a critical request was rejected by the user.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I am suggesting a new synchronous method like `ShowSync` which returns the error and result from either callback function assigned to the buttons.

If feasible, we could also introduce generics so that the result returned from the cancel or default buttons are type safe.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

The current implementation in v3 is asynchronous. The v2 implementation was synchronous and similar to the above request. However, the callbacks will be called to return result or error instead simply returning the button labels as the result.

### Additional context

_No response_

items.title: Windows NSIS, Shortcuts for Non-Admin Users
items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

When a Non-Admin user installs the Wails-App using Wail's default NSIS installer file, there are neither desktop nor program links created for the user. 

My understanding of what is happening:

- RequestExecutionLevel is 'admin'.
- SetShellVarContext default value is 'current'. As 'current' is 'admin', only the admin does get program links.



### Describe the solution you'd like

The default NSIS should add `SetShellVarContext all` in the installer section and the uninstaller section, just before 'CreateShortcut' and 'Delete'.

/build/windows/installer/poject.nsi
```
...
Section
    !insertmacro wails.webview2runtime

    SetOutPath $INSTDIR
    
    !insertmacro wails.files
    SetShellVarContext all
    CreateShortcut "$SMPROGRAMS\${INFO_PRODUCTNAME}.lnk" "$INSTDIR\${PRODUCT_EXECUTABLE}"
    CreateShortCut "$DESKTOP\${INFO_PRODUCTNAME}.lnk" "$INSTDIR\${PRODUCT_EXECUTABLE}"

    !insertmacro wails.writeUninstaller
SectionEnd

Section "uninstall" 
    RMDir /r "$AppData\${PRODUCT_EXECUTABLE}" # Remove the WebView2 DataPath

    RMDir /r $INSTDIR

    SetShellVarContext all
    Delete "$SMPROGRAMS\${INFO_PRODUCTNAME}.lnk"
    Delete "$DESKTOP\${INFO_PRODUCTNAME}.lnk"

    !insertmacro wails.deleteUninstaller
SectionEnd
```

### Describe alternatives you've considered

I have tried to set 

```
RequestExecutionLevel user
```
However, then the non-admin user could not install the app because of no write access to C:\Program Files.


### Additional context

_No response_

items.title: [v2] Custom menu disables clipboard shortcuts in text inputs (macOS)
items.body:
### Description

When a custom menu is set via `Menu: appMenu` in `main.go`, standard text input shortcuts stop working. In this repro app, `Cmd/Ctrl+V`, `Cmd/Ctrl+A`, and `Cmd/Ctrl+C` do not work in the input. If I comment out `Menu: appMenu`, the shortcuts work again.

### To Reproduce

1. `wails init -n wails-menu-input-bug -t vanilla`
2. Add a custom menu and set `Menu: appMenu` in `main.go` ([see repro repo](https://github.com/beam-transfer/wails-menu-bug/blob/main/main.go#L60-L62)).
3. `wails dev`
4. Click the input field.
5. Try `Cmd/Ctrl+V`, `Cmd/Ctrl+A`, `Cmd/Ctrl+C`.
6. Comment out `Menu: appMenu`, restart, and try again.

### Expected behaviour

Clipboard shortcuts should work in text inputs even when a custom menu is set.

### Screenshots

N/A (text input shortcut issue).

### Attempted Fixes

- Commented out `Menu: appMenu` → shortcuts work.
- Created minimal repro app and simplified menu structure.

items.title: [v3][darwin] Zoom In/Out/Reset and SetZoom magnify the web view instead of zooming the page — no reflow, content clipped, unlike Windows, Linux and Safari

milestone.title: Future
milestone.description: Unscheduled feature work beyond GA. Placement here is not a commitment to a specific release. Goose should move items to a numbered milestone only when that release scope is justified.

items.body:
## Environment - Wails v3.0.0-beta.27 — the macOS zoom code is unchanged since v3's first commit (`81645190f0`, 2023-01), so every beta behaves the same; also reproduced on `master` at 3a83b2c65b (2026-10-05) - macOS 27.0 (26A428), darwin/arm64, Go 1.27.1 ## Description On macOS `Window.ZoomIn()`, `ZoomOut()`, `ZoomReset()`, `SetZoom()` and `GetZoom()` — and with them the `ZoomIn` / `ZoomOut` / `ResetZoom` menu roles, i.e. ⌘+ / ⌘− / ⌘0 in the View menu that `NewViewMenu()` builds — are implemented with `-[WKWebView setMagnification:]` (`windowZoomIn` & co. in `v3/pkg/application/webview_window_darwin.go`). `magnification` is a view-level scale transform, the pinch-to-zoom kind: the page keeps its layout viewport, is drawn larger, and whatever no longer fits is cut off at the right and bottom edges (it can be scrolled into view). Nothing reflows — text keeps its line breaks, responsive layouts keep their breakpoints, elements anchored to the right edge leave the window. The other two backends implement the same API as a *browser zoom*: Windows through `ICoreWebView2Controller::put_ZoomFactor`, Linux through `webkit_web_view_set_zoom_level`. There the CSS viewport shrinks, text wraps and the layout adapts — what ⌘+ does in Safari, Chrome, Edge or any Electron app, and what users expect from the shortcut. macOS is the odd one out. WKWebView has had the browser-zoom equivalent since macOS 11: [`pageZoom`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/webkit/wkwebview/pagezoom). It is what Safari's View → Zoom In drives, and it leaves `magnification` to the pinch gesture (`AllowsMagnification`). ## To Reproduce Interactively: any app with the default View menu and a page of wrapping text — press ⌘+ a few times. The right part of the page disappears and a horizontal scrollbar shows up instead of the text re-wrapping. Programmatically — an 800 px window with a long paragraph; 1.5 s after start Go calls `ZoomIn()` six times (→ 1.30), then `ZoomReset()`, and after each step the page reports its viewport metrics back through the asset handler: `main.go` ```go package main import ( _ "embed" "fmt" "net/http" "os" "time" "github.com/wailsapp/wails/v3/pkg/application" ) //go:embed index.html var index []byte func main() { mux := http.NewServeMux() mux.HandleFunc("/", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/html") w.Write(index) }) mux.HandleFunc("/report", func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) { fmt.Println("page:", r.URL.RawQuery) }) app := application.New(application.Options{ Name: "zoomrepro", Assets: application.AssetOptions{Handler: mux}, }) window := app.Window.NewWithOptions(application.WebviewWindowOptions{URL: "/", Width: 800, Height: 500}) go func() { time.Sleep(1500 * time.Millisecond) report(window, "initial") for i := 0; i < 6; i++ { window.ZoomIn() } time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond) fmt.Printf("GetZoom=%.2f\n", window.GetZoom()) report(window, "zoomed") window.ZoomReset() time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond) report(window, "reset") time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond) app.Quit() }() if err := app.Run(); err != nil { fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err) os.Exit(1) } } func report(window *application.WebviewWindow, tag string) { window.ExecJS(fmt.Sprintf(`fetch('/report?' + new URLSearchParams({ tag: %q, innerWidth: innerWidth, clientWidth: document.documentElement.clientWidth, vvWidth: Math.round(visualViewport.width), vvScale: visualViewport.scale.toFixed(2), lines: document.getElementById('p').getClientRects().length, rightEdge: Math.round(document.getElementById('r').getBoundingClientRect().right), }))`, tag)) time.Sleep(400 * time.Millisecond) } ``` `index.html` (the runtime is loaded only because `ExecJS` is queued until it is) ```html
LEFT EDGERIGHT EDGE

The layout viewport never changes: the page is scaled, not zoomed, and 185 CSS px of it are clipped. ## Expected behaviour The same as on Windows and Linux and in Safari: the layout viewport shrinks to 800 / 1.3 ≈ 615 CSS px, text reflows, nothing is clipped. With the five zoom functions switched to `pageZoom` (see below) the same run gives: | | `documentElement.clientWidth` | `visualViewport.width` | `visualViewport.scale` | lines in the paragraph | right-edge marker | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | after 6 × `ZoomIn()` | 616 | 615 | 1.00 | 13 | 591 — visible | `GetZoom()` still reports 1.30 and `ZoomReset()` returns every value to the initial row. ## Recordings Two screen recordings of the same app, ⌘+ pressed a few times. **Before** — current behaviour, `setMagnification:`: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/615ffa23-e985-4b7b-8505-d8a5a876f41f **After** — the same app zooming through `WKWebView.pageZoom`: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12b3c712-2848-4291-8cf9-f8827eaaa2c9 ## Attempted Fixes Replacing `setMagnification:` / `magnification` with `pageZoom` in `windowZoomReset` / `windowZoomSet` / `windowZoomGet` / `windowZoomIn` / `windowZoomOut` behind `if (@available(macOS 11.0, *))`, with the old magnification path as the fallback (the package still compiles with `-mmacosx-version-min=10.13`), and letting `windowZoomReset` reset the magnification as well so a pinch zoom still returns to actual size on ⌘0. That is the "expected" table above; PR to follow. items.title: Support showing window in all workspaces on MacOS
items.body:
### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Hey!
Just let me start by saying that Wails is incredible!

Anyway, I'd like to create an app on MacOS that works like Spotlight / Alfred, so basically is invokable through a shortcut and shows up on the current workspace (virtual desktop). I couldn't seem to find that in the Wails API.

### Describe the solution you'd like

I took a look at how Electron does it, and it seems they didn't solve it directly (haven't added support for the workspaces API) but one user posted a workaround that just shows the window on all workspaces: https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/8734#issuecomment-350145566

It'd be great to have that API call available. I'm not well-versed in the MacOS-specific APIs, but it seems to be similar to the current API calls like SetAlwaysOnTop.

(the related issue https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/5362 mentions why they didn't add support for the actual workspaces API, btw)
